run.head: d86d230
run.note: Conflict resolution round on PR #1594 (feat/stream-input-priority-latest-frame) after main landed #1605 (daemon idle timeout). Gate scoped to the merge resolution plus the full branch diff.

lenses.name: Inverse regression surface
lenses.reason: Merge removed handle_client_message; checked that every behavior it carried (input dispatch, idle marking) survives in reader_loop.

lenses.name: New-domain matrix
lenses.reason: maxFps domain re-driven post-merge: 0 (uncapped), 2, 10, 30, plus negative/string/oversized covered by unit tests.

lenses.name: Resolution-rule consistency across consumers
lenses.reason: Enumerated every consumer of the idle-activity rule: daemon startup, handle_stream_enable, WS reader. All three wire the daemon-owned Arc.

lenses.name: Emission channel and one-shot latch reachability
lenses.reason: frame_watch is a latest-value latch; verified borrow_and_update at send time, not arrival time, and that the seeded initial frame is marked seen.

lenses.name: Shim hermeticity
lenses.reason: No shim, wrapper, or launcher in the diff.

lenses.name: Deliberate-default check
lenses.reason: Default maxFps 0 (uncapped) preserves pre-PR behavior for clients that never send config.

lenses.name: Fresh-seam scan
lenses.reason: The merge itself is the fresh seam: reader task vs writer loop lifecycle, and the new idle-activity crossing between them.

lenses.name: Reference-implementation oracle
lenses.reason: No upstream reference implementation; independent reimplementation per PR body.

lenses.name: New-failure-outcome propagation
lenses.reason: reader_task completion now terminates the writer loop; verified cleanup (client_count decrement, notify) still runs on that path.

lenses.name: Flag-propagation dispatch sweep
lenses.reason: No CLI flag added; config is a WS protocol message.

lenses.name: Error-path forcing
lenses.reason: ws send error on both the throttled and broadcast arms breaks the loop; exercised by client disconnect during streaming.

lenses.name: Non-destructive recovery
lenses.reason: Diff writes no persistent state.

lenses.name: Cancellation and timeout hygiene
lenses.reason: reader_task.abort() on every writer-loop exit; shutdown_rx arm sends Close first. No orphaned task on any break path.

lenses.name: Boundary pipeline trace
lenses.reason: Traced CDP screencast frame to WS text frame across the new watch channel; ack-immediately semantics in cdp_loop.rs unchanged by the merge.

lenses.name: Substrate verification
lenses.reason: Driven against real Chrome 151 over CDP, not mocks.

lenses.name: Dogfood the built artifact
lenses.reason: Release binary built from the merged branch and driven: maxFps throttling measured, clicks landed on a real page, idle seam A/B tested against a separately built origin/main binary.

lenses.name: Docs-behavior parity
lenses.reason: README, docs/src/app/streaming/page.mdx, and stream --help all describe latest-first delivery and maxFps 1-120 / 0; measured behavior matches.

lenses.name: Demonstrative example
lenses.reason: docs carry a config message example; verified the exact payload shape works against the binary.

lenses.name: Choice audit
lenses.reason: No decision trail recorded for this change.

lenses.name: Complexity budget
lenses.reason: Merge resolution adds one function parameter and one guarded call; no new abstraction.

deterministic.reason: zero hits; the function main deleted-into is fully retired

Four call sites outside the diff, all of two unrelated same-named private functions (daemon.rs:503, inspect_server.rs:97). The stream module's handle_connection is private and called only from websocket.rs:81, inside the diff. Gate matches on bare symbol name and cannot see module scope.
Not run; the operator interrupted the invocation. Map is a ranking aid, not a gate, and every lens ran on the full diff without it.

findings.claim: The merge resolution marked idle activity before the CDP client guard, silently widening #1605's semantics: dashboard input on a session with no attached client would defer daemon idle shutdown, which main never did.
findings.evidence: Pre-merge main marked inside `if let Some(ref client) = *guard` in handle_client_message (websocket.rs, origin/main). The first resolution hoisted the mark above the guard in reader_loop. Fixed in d86d230 by moving the mark inside the guard; 1033 tests, clippy, and fmt green after.
findings.layer: merge semantics of an adjacent PR's contract
findings.path: reader_loop -> IdleActivity::mark -> daemon idle select loop

findings.claim: Feature behavior survives the merge intact: per-client maxFps throttling and immediate input dispatch both work on the merged binary.
findings.evidence: Release binary from d86d230 against Chrome 151 on an rAF-animating page: maxFps=0 -> 181 frames/3s, maxFps=2 -> 6, maxFps=10 -> 30, maxFps=30 -> 87. Three WS mousePressed/mouseReleased pairs produced clicks=3 read back via eval on the page.

findings.claim: A connected stream WebSocket client defers daemon idle shutdown indefinitely even with zero user input, so #1605's idle timeout does not fire for any session with a dashboard attached.
findings.evidence: AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=8000, daemon pid resolved via lsof on the stream port. No WS client: daemon EXITED by t=14s. WS client connected receiving frames only, no input, 20s: ALIVE. Identical on a separately built origin/main binary (/tmp/ab-main-idle), so this predates the branch.

exemptions.claim: The four out-of-diff handle_connection call sites do not need reading for this change.
exemptions.evidence: grep -rn 'fn handle_connection' returns three distinct private functions in three modules; the stream one at websocket.rs:120 has exactly one caller, websocket.rs:81, which is inside the diff.

exemptions.claim: Skipping the Impact Map does not leave the review under-covered.
exemptions.evidence: The diff spans six files in one subsystem, all read in full during the lens passes; the map ranks propagation but adds no reachable symbol the passes did not already cover.

issue_candidates.title: Stream WS client with no input keeps the daemon alive past its idle timeout
issue_candidates.evidence: See F3. Reproduced on origin/main (3cc7022) with the shipped 8s-override path; no-WS control exits on schedule.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: Pre-existing in #1605, reproduced identically on main; PR #1594 neither introduces nor worsens it. Fixing it means deciding whether a connected dashboard counts as activity, which is a lifecycle policy call for the #1605 author.
